builder_plan.scenario: A narrow, repeated product task may not need your largest model.
builder_plan.change: Check whether a released student model fits the task before generating training data.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current model and an off-the-shelf small model on the same held-out tasks.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Student quality, serving cost, teacher calls, training cost, and failures on unusual inputs.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: From LoRA to Language: Recovering Skill Documents from Adapters
summary: The method replaces opaque, non-portable LoRA skill adapters with readable, editable, model-agnostic skill documents regenerated either by a small writer model trained over the adapted base or by an agent that diffs base-versus-adapter behavior. It costs training data and compute for the writer (or extra inference runs for the differential agent), adds a pipeline stage, and yields a document that captures only a fraction of the original instructions. It fails when the adapter was trained on behavior alone rather than on the document (1-2% instruction recovery), when the adapter's behavior is already guessable from the base model (a reward loop without the adapter performs equally well), and weight-only reading approaches transmit about one bit.
rationale: For a constrained team using LoRA-compiled skills, the differential agent approach is cheap enough to validate on their own adapters, but recovery quality depends heavily on how the adapter was trained, so it warrants workload-specific testing rather than adoption.
technique: Recovering skill documents from LoRA adapters

claims.statement: The method replaces opaque, non-portable LoRA skill adapters with readable, editable, model-agnostic skill documents regenerated either by a small writer model trained over the adapted base or by an agent that diffs base-versus-adapter behavior. It costs training data and compute for the writer (or extra inference runs for the differential agent), adds a pipeline stage, and yields a document that captures only a fraction of the original instructions. It fails when the adapter was trained on behavior alone rather than on the document (1-2% instruction recovery), when the adapter's behavior is already guessable from the base model (a reward loop without the adapter performs equally well), and weight-only reading approaches transmit about one bit.

The trained Executing Writer recovers 39-44% of key instructions from held-out skill adapters; recovered documents restore 85-91% of the original skill's task gain on 41 external skills; agent-written skills recover 58-71% of a LoRA's gain on ALFWorld and lift Llama-3.1-8B from 5% to 55% task success.
